concepts.label: Sync Gateway 4.1.0
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused within batch (also minted in compatibility.json) - this page's release-notes heading for the described features

concepts.label: Cluster Compatibility Version (Sync Gateway 4.1+)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new Sync-Gateway-4.1-specific mechanism, not in the registry: a per-cluster version marker that lets nodes at different code versions coexist safely during a rolling upgrade

concepts.label: Non-Disruptive Rolling Upgrade (Sync Gateway 4.1+)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the named 4.1 feature enabling node-by-node upgrades without downtime, distinct from (and reliant on) sgw:cluster-compatibility-version

concepts.label: Distributed Resync (Sync Gateway 4.1+)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a redesign of the already-promoted sgw:resync-operation to distribute work in parallel across all cluster nodes; kept as a distinct concept rather than folded into sgw:resync-operation since the source explicitly frames it as replacing 'the previous single-node sequential approach', i.e. a version-specific architectural change to that operation, not merely a synonym

concepts.label: Channel History Management (Sync Gateway 4.1+)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new Admin REST API endpoints (4.1) for retrieving/pruning channel history on user records and documents; genuinely new capability, not previously in the registry

concepts.label: Metadata migration to _system._mobile (Sync Gateway 4.1+)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already-promoted concept, matched almost verbatim by this page's own description of the opt-in, one-way migration

relations.subject: sgw:non-disruptive-rolling-upgrade
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway 4.1 introduces cluster compatibility version, enabling node-by-node upgrades without downtime, with a safe rollback path throughout the upgrade window.

relations.subject: sgw:non-disruptive-rolling-upgrade
relations.evidence: Version 4.1 of Sync Gateway delivers the following features and enhancements.

relations.subject: sgw:distributed-resync
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway 4.1 redesigns resync to distribute work in parallel across all cluster nodes, replacing the previous single-node sequential approach.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-history-management
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway 4.1 introduces Admin REST API endpoints for retrieving and pruning channel history on both user records and documents, reducing metadata bloat and unnecessary revocation messages during zero-checkpoint replications.

relations.subject: sgw:metadata-migration-to-system-collection
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway 4.1 introduces an opt-in migration that moves Sync Gateway internal metadata from `_default._default` to `_system._mobile`, isolating it from user application data. The migration is never applied automatically at upgrade and cannot be reversed.

relations.subject: sync-gateway/4.1/product-notes/release-notes
relations.evidence: The migration to a 4.x configuration is a ONE WAY process — see: [Upgrading](../upgrading.md) for more.

notable_absence.finding: This page's Enhancements list (CBG-4363 'Enable xattr only DCP stream for Sync Gateway caching feed', CBG-4542 'Skip revcache insertion on all write operations', CBG-5091 'Increase websocket control frame timeouts') consists of Jira-ticket-title-only entries with no prose explanation of mechanism or version-gating on this page - so unlike the three headline features (rolling upgrades, distributed resync, channel history), these could not be extracted into relations beyond noting them exist. The release-notes format for enhancements is systematically less extractable than for headline features: a bare ticket title carries no evidence sentence a relation could quote.

cross_component_finding: The 'Enhancements' list separately names CBG-5206 'Cluster Compatibility and Rolling Upgrade Enhancements' and CBG-5221 'System scoped metadata and online migration process' as engineering-ticket-level entries that duplicate, at the Jira-ticket granularity, the same two headline features (Non-Disruptive Rolling Upgrades, Metadata Isolation) already described in prose earlier on the same page - the page documents each 4.1 headline feature twice, once as a prose section with a cross-reference link and once as a terse enhancement-list bullet, with no link between the two.
cross_product_finding: Fixed issue CBG-4939 ('Couchbase Lite 4.0 is allowed to connect to Sync Gateway 3.2.6/3.3.0') is the engineering-side confirmation of the exact compatibility warning stated as a product-level WARNING box on compatibility.md ('Couchbase Lite 4.0 with Sync Gateway 3.2.0 and 3.3.0 is unsupported') - the same cross-product incompatibility appears independently on two pages in this batch, in two different registers (a bug-fix log entry here, a compatibility-matrix warning there), corroborating version:sgw-3-3-0 and version:cbl-4-0 as genuinely load-bearing ids rather than one-off mentions.
